Research, experiments and new AI methods

Science & Research track

The gap between a promising result and something you can actually use is where this track lives. New methods, honest evaluation, experiments that did not go as planned, and the research coming out of the North's knowledge institutions that could be practically applicable sooner than you think.

📅 November 13, 2026 📍 Groningen city center
Track champions
About the track

What is emerging now, and what it could mean soon.

This track is aimed at researchers, scientists, doctoral candidates, students, research-and-development teams and knowledge institutions: people who care as much about the method as the result.

The speakers are researchers, scientists, doctoral candidates and R&D practitioners presenting new findings, methods or experiments. Expect evaluation you can scrutinise, societal impact taken seriously, and applied research done together with industry or the public sector.

Seven talks, or a deliberate combination of talks, posters and demos.

Scientific results Methods Experiments Evaluation Societal impact Applied research Industry collaboration Public-sector collaboration
Track at a glance
  • Theme Research, experiments and new Artificial Intelligence methods
  • For Researchers, scientists, doctoral candidates, students, research and development teams and knowledge institutions
  • Format Seven talks, or a deliberate combination of talks, posters and demos
  • Date Friday November 13, 2026 · Groningen
  • Track champions University of Groningen — Jantina Tammes School, and TNO

Call for proposals

Presenting something new?

We are looking for researchers, scientists, doctoral candidates and research-and-development speakers with new findings, methods or experiments to put in front of a curious, mixed audience.

Negative results and methods that did not survive contact with reality are welcome too. Submit your proposal for aiGrunn 2026 and join a lineup of speakers from across the Netherlands and beyond.

Submit your talk →

Deadline for submissions: 13 October 2026

What we are looking for
  • New findings, methods, experiments or evaluation approaches, explained for a mixed technical audience
  • Applied research and collaborations with industry or the public sector are especially welcome
  • Posters and demos are an option alongside talks: tell us what fits your work
  • No sales pitches. All talks must deliver genuine learning value
  • Slots: 30 minutes including Q&A
  • English submissions only
  • All talks are recorded and published on YouTube
